document.abstract: In the Middle Ages, a young man who wished to become a doctor of medicine, was able to select his own teachers. Having heard for instance, of the reputation of a famous surgeon, say in Padua, he went there and served an apprenticeship until he had learned all that doctor could teach him. Then he travelled on to the next authority, making his selection according to what he felt was necessary to make him a good practitioner. (Fig. 1)

authors.affiliation: Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto Toronto, Ont.
authors.bio: J. Norrie Swanson, M.D., F.R.C.P. (Ed.), 40 Wellesley St. East, Suite 402, Toronto 5, is currently President, Health Sciences Communications Association and a member of the Board of Directors of the Ontario Educational Communications Authority. He is also a consultant on Audio-Visual Education to the Toronto Teaching Hospitals. Dr. Swanson has been the Director, Audio-Visual Resources Div., Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto; Chairman; Subcommittee of Audio-Visual Systems, Ontario Council of Health; and President, Canadian Association for the study of Instructional Media and Medical Education.
